question.text: Consider the real valued function $\mathrm{h}:\{0,1,2 \ldots \ldots 100\} \rightarrow \mathrm{R}$ such that $\mathrm{h}(0)=5, \mathrm{~h}(100)=20$ and satisfying $h(p)=\frac{1}{2}\{h(p+1)+h(p-1)\}$ for every $p=1,2 \ldots .99 .$ Then the value of $h(1)$ is

solution.text:
$h(p)=\frac{1}{2}(h(p+1)+h(p-1)) \Rightarrow h(p-1), h(p), h(p+1)$ are in A.P.
$h(100)=h(0)+99 d$
$\Rightarrow \frac{20-5}{99}=d \Rightarrow d=\frac{15}{99} \Rightarrow h(1)=h(0)+d=5+\frac{15}{99}=5.15$
